image.name: Lighthouse
image.subsector: Commercial and industrial distributed solar and solar-plus-storage
image.description: Lighthouse is a portfolio of 38 operating commercial-and-industrial distributed solar and solar-plus-storage projects totaling 89 MWDC across California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Vermont and Washington. The portfolio is asset-heavy and contracted, with operating renewable-generation and storage assets serving long-term commercial and industrial offtakers. BlackRock's Evergreen infrastructure strategy signed to acquire Lighthouse in November 2023 and the sale closed in December 2023. Excelsior Energy Capital sold 100% of its membership interests in the portfolio through Excelsior Renewable Energy Investment Fund I LP and disclosed the completed exit in March 2024. The transaction disclosure does not establish that BlackRock owns 100% of every project's total economic interests, so the current platform-level percentage is not inferred. Lighthouse is counted once as the manager-level portfolio; its 38 underlying project and SPV assets are not separate PortCos. No later portfolio sale, transfer or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 23, 2026.

This supports the disclosed fund attribution and existing curated Evergreen Infrastructure Fund link, not a separately named legal holding entity. The signing release is not proof of closing or a 100% project-level economic stake; preserve the canonical December 2023 closing and the distinction between all of Excelsior's membership interests and undisclosed total project-level economic ownership.

image.name: Permanent Power Company
image.subsector: Utility-scale solar, battery storage and transmission
image.description: Permanent Power Company is a CIM Group-backed U.S. power-infrastructure platform that owns and develops utility-scale solar generation, battery storage and transmission assets. SEC filings identify Permanent Power Company, LLC as the renamed former Westlands Electric Power Company, LLC. At March 31, 2026, CIM Opportunity Zone Fund held approximately 66.7% of the company, including its direct interest and the interest held through COZ 1, while other CIM-affiliated entities held the remaining 33.3%. CIM launched the Permanent Power brand in May 2026 with 652 MW of operating solar, 360 MW/1,440 MWh of battery storage and 15 miles of transmission, plus the Grape and Daylight projects in construction or construction-ready development. Westlands Solar Park is the California site/master plan beneath Permanent Power, and Aquamarine is its first 250 MW utility-scale solar project rather than a separate portfolio company. The Westlands development lineage began in 2014, construction started in 2020 and Aquamarine entered commercial operation in late 2021. The exact rename effective date, company headquarters and identities within the 33.3% CIM-affiliate block are not publicly disclosed. No third-party sale, change of control or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

milestones.event: Aquamarine, the first 250 MW utility-scale solar project within Westlands Solar Park, entered commercial operation.
CIM affiliates completed phased contributions of power-project interests into WEPCO; the CIM Opportunity Zone Fund interest reached approximately 66.7% and other CIM affiliates held 33.3%.
CIM Group announced the formation of Westlands Electric Power Company as the consolidated owner of its contributed California power assets.
An SEC filing identified Permanent Power Company, LLC as the former Westlands Electric Power Company, LLC and reported the 66.7%/33.3% CIM-affiliate ownership split.

CIM launched Permanent Power Company as its national power-infrastructure platform and disclosed the operating solar, storage and transmission portfolio plus the Grape and Daylight expansion projects.
CIM Group and a joint-venture partner obtained rights to acquire more than 20,000 acres for the Westlands Solar Park clean-energy development.
CIM publicly described Westlands Solar Park as a fully permitted clean-energy development with more than 2,700 MW of potential capacity across over 20,000 acres in California's Central Valley.
CIM announced the start of construction at Westlands Solar Park, then described as a permitted development with more than 2,700 MW of potential capacity.
WEPCO reported a seven-asset contributed power portfolio at year-end 2025, comprising five operational assets and two construction-ready assets.

state.attributionRationale: SEC filings directly identify CIM Opportunity Zone Fund, L.P. as holding the controlling 66.7% economic interest, including its direct interest and the interest held through COZ 1. No matching normalized fund row exists, so preserve the disclosed vehicle without inferring CIM Infrastructure Fund III.

CIM's Westlands development history supports the former CIM and joint-venture ownership period, but the reviewed public evidence does not identify a specific CIM fund or the joint-venture partner. Remove the unsupported CIM Infrastructure Fund I inference while preserving the historical ownership period.
